name: Beacon Analytics
positioning: Enterprise-first. Lands via platform teams, expands to product org.

pages.title: Beacon Analytics — Pricing
pages.text: Beacon is priced per tracked user with an annual commitment. The Starter tier is capped at 10k monthly tracked users and excludes data export. Growth adds warehouse sync and 90-day retention. Enterprise unlocks unlimited retention, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and a dedicated success manager. All tiers meter overages at $0.12 per additional tracked user. Annual prepay is required above Starter; there is no month-to-month option on Growth or Enterprise.

pages.title: Beacon Docs — Quickstart
pages.text: Install the Beacon SDK and initialize with your project key. Beacon requires an explicit identify() call before any event is attributed to a user; anonymous events are dropped after 24 hours unless stitching is enabled. Server-side ingestion is available on Growth and above via the HTTP API. The SDK adds roughly 34kb gzipped to a web bundle.

pages.title: Beacon Docs — Rate limits and quotas
pages.text: The ingestion API accepts 1,000 events per second per project. Bursts above the limit return 429 and are not retried by the SDK. Warehouse sync runs every 6 hours on Growth and every hour on Enterprise; real-time sync is not offered. Custom properties are capped at 40 per event.

pricing.notes: Warehouse sync every 6h, 90-day retention, annual prepay
SSO/SAML, audit logs, unlimited retention, custom contract

reviews.quote: Rock solid ingestion and the warehouse sync just works. Pricing gets painful the moment you cross a tracked-user tier — we jumped 3x in one renewal.
Powerful but heavy. Onboarding took our platform team most of a quarter, and the required identify() call broke attribution on our marketing site for weeks.
Beacon is what you buy when procurement wants SOC2 and a CSM on speed dial. Not what you buy when you want to ship something Friday.
